observatories.name: Maunakea Observatories
observatories.description: A group of independent observatories on the summit of Maunakea, at about 4,205 m, observing in optical, infrared and submillimeter wavelengths. Twelve facilities house thirteen telescopes with mirrors from 0.9 to 25 m, including the twin Keck telescopes, Subaru and the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope.
highlights: The University of Hawaii 2.24 m telescope had first light in 1970, starting the site's growth as an international observatory.
Keck I had first light on 24 November 1990 and Keck II on 27 April 1996; each has a mirror of 36 hexagonal segments.
Research here contributed to the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics for the accelerating expansion of the universe.

observatories.name: Paranal Observatory and the Very Large Telescope
observatories.place: Cerro Paranal, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region
observatories.description: ESO's observatory on Cerro Paranal at 2,635 m, home of the Very Large Telescope: four 8.2 m telescopes that can also work together as an interferometer, plus four 1.8 m auxiliary telescopes. It also hosts the VISTA and VLT Survey Telescopes.
highlights: Beta Pictoris b, imaged in 2008, is described as the first direct image of an exoplanet.
The VLT tracked stars orbiting the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, and in 2018 measured gravitational redshift there, a test of general relativity.
It observed the afterglow of GRB 090423, the furthest known gamma-ray burst.

observatories.name: La Silla Observatory
observatories.place: La Silla, Coquimbo Region (Atacama Desert edge)
observatories.description: ESO's first observatory in Chile, at 2,400 m under some of the darkest skies on Earth. Its main telescopes are the ESO 3.6 m, the New Technology Telescope and the MPG/ESO 2.2 m.
highlights: The HARPS spectrograph is described as the most successful finder of low-mass exoplanets to date.
HARPS found planets in the Gliese 581 system, including what may be the first known rocky planet in a habitable zone outside the Solar System.
La Silla followed SN 1987A, the nearest recent supernova, from 1987.

observatories.name: Vera C. Rubin Observatory
observatories.description: A US NSF-DOE facility on Cerro Pachón with the 8.4 m Simonyi Survey Telescope and the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera. It images the whole southern sky every few nights.
highlights: Its 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time began in July 2026.
The LSST Camera is described as the largest digital camera ever built.
The survey is expected to catalog millions of supernovae and more than five million asteroids.

observatories.name: Extremely Large Telescope
observatories.description: ESO's 39.3 m segmented-mirror telescope under construction on Cerro Armazones at 3,046 m, about 23 km from Paranal. First light is expected in March 2029.
highlights: Its primary mirror has 798 hexagonal segments and a collecting area of 978 square meters.
Construction started in June 2014 and passed the halfway point in July 2023.
Goals include finding extrasolar planets and characterizing their atmospheres.

observatories.name: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
observatories.place: Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma, Canary Islands
observatories.description: An observatory of the Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias on La Palma, opened in 1985, hosting telescopes from Britain, the Netherlands, Spain and other countries. Its largest is the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias.
highlights: The Gran Telescopio Canarias had first light on 13 July 2007 and was inaugurated on 24 July 2009 by King Juan Carlos I.
It was described as the world's largest single-aperture optical telescope, with 36 hexagonal mirror segments.
The site also has the William Herschel Telescope and the Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope with adaptive optics.

observatories.name: Palomar Observatory
observatories.place: Palomar Mountain, San Diego County, California
observatories.description: A Caltech observatory in the Palomar Mountains, home of the 200-inch (5.1 m) Hale Telescope. Smaller telescopes there support the Zwicky Transient Facility.
highlights: The Hale Telescope had first light on 26 January 1949, with Edwin Hubble pointing it at NGC 2261.
It was the world's largest optical telescope until the Soviet BTA-6 was built (Wikipedia's Hale article says 1976, its Palomar article says 1975).
Quasars were identified as high-redshift sources from Hale Telescope spectra.

observatories.name: Mount Wilson Observatory
observatories.place: Mount Wilson, San Gabriel Mountains, California
observatories.description: A historic observatory above Los Angeles, first funded by the Carnegie Institution in 1904, with the 100-inch Hooker telescope (completed 1917) and the CHARA interferometer array. It now combines research with public tours and observing nights.
highlights: In 1923 Edwin Hubble showed with the Hooker telescope that the Andromeda nebula lies outside the Milky Way.
In 1929 Hubble and Milton Humason demonstrated that the universe is expanding.
The 100-inch was the world's largest telescope until 1949.

observatories.name: Observatoire de Haute-Provence
observatories.description: A French national observatory established in 1937 near Saint-Michel-l'Observatoire, at about 650 m. It operates 1.93 m, 1.52 m, 1.20 m and 0.80 m reflecting telescopes.
highlights: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz found the planet orbiting 51 Pegasi using ELODIE on the 1.93 m telescope.
That discovery earned them half of the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Observations began in 1943 with the 1.20 m telescope.

observatories.name: Southern African Large Telescope
observatories.description: A 9.2 m optical telescope near Sutherland in the Karoo at 1,798 m, designed mainly for spectroscopy, with 91 hexagonal mirror segments. It is operated by the South African Astronomical Observatory.
highlights: First light was on 1 September 2005; President Thabo Mbeki inaugurated it on 10 November 2005.
It is described as the largest optical telescope in the Southern Hemisphere.
It is used to study black holes, supernovae, binary stars and compact stars.

observatories.name: LAMOST (Guo Shoujing Telescope) at Xinglong Observatory
observatories.description: The Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope, also called the Guo Shoujing Telescope, at Xinglong Station. About 4000 optical fibers on its focal surface let it take thousands of spectra per night.
highlights: It was planned to survey the spectra of 10 million Milky Way stars plus millions of galaxies.
Its data releases began in June 2013, and the official site lists a public DR11 release.
It runs two surveys: LEGAS (extragalactic) and LEGUE (Galactic).

observatories.name: Devasthal Observatory
observatories.description: An observatory of ARIES at 2,450 m near Nainital in Uttarakhand. Its main instrument is the 3.6 m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT).
highlights: The 3.6 m DOT had first light on 31 March 2016.
It is described as the largest reflecting telescope in Asia and the first in India with an active optics system.
It was built by ARIES with the Belgian firm AMOS making the optics.

observatories.name: BTA-6 at the Special Astrophysical Observatory
observatories.description: The 6 m Large Altazimuth Telescope (BTA-6) of the Special Astrophysical Observatory of the Russian Academy of Sciences, set up in 1966, in the Caucasus foothills.
highlights: BTA-6 had first light in 1975 (Wikipedia's BTA-6 article says late 1975).
For years it was the world's largest single-primary-mirror optical reflector, until Keck 1 in 1993.
It surpassed the Hale Telescope, which had been the largest for 26 years.
